review_basis: registered MHLW model SDS Section 9 autoignition and explosion-range fields
all 205 canonical/source-verified Otsu4 questions including Wave 1 flash-point properties
semantic distinctness, fire-hazard practice value and no-filler policy

decisions.rationale: Gasoline autoignition temperature is a new ignition-property fact and does not duplicate the canonical gasoline flash-point item.
The gasoline lower explosion limit is a source-explicit hazard boundary not represented in canonical 205.
The gasoline upper explosion limit is the independent upper boundary paired with C002 and is not interchangeable with the lower limit.
The stem supplies both gasoline explosion limits, reducing the task to a simple midpoint interval check; C016 retains the stronger representative concentration-to-boundary application.
Ethanol autoignition temperature adds a substance-specific ignition property distinct from its verified flash-point recall.
The ethanol lower explosion limit is a distinct source-bound property with practical flammability value.
The ethanol upper explosion limit is a separate boundary from C006 and materially differs from the gasoline range.
This repeats C004's supplied-range midpoint classification with an ethanol substance swap and adds insufficient incremental practice value.
Methanol autoignition temperature is a new substance-specific ignition property distinct from the canonical methanol flash point.
The methanol lower explosion limit is a distinct source-explicit flammability boundary.
The methanol upper explosion limit is independently useful and materially broader than its lower boundary.
This is the third supplied-range midpoint classification and adds only a substance/numeric swap after the same reasoning path.
Acetone autoignition temperature is a new ignition property and is distinct from the verified acetone flash-point question.
The acetone lower explosion limit is a source-specific lower flammability boundary not present in canonical 205.
The acetone upper explosion limit is the independent upper boundary paired with C014.
Unlike the rejected midpoint variants, this tests recognition that a concentration above the same-source upper explosion limit lies outside the range on the high side.
Comparing gasoline flash point with autoignition temperature tests the important concept distinction using one SDS and does not re-ask the flash-point value alone.
The acetone version repeats C017's identical flash-point-versus-autoignition comparison and adds only a substance swap.

collision_review.note: Canonical Wave 1 flash-point recalls are not recreated as standalone flash questions. Four repeated derived reasoning paths are rejected; the remaining 14 add autoignition or explosion-range properties or one representative concept distinction.

source_review_scope: This gate checks source registration, locator reproducibility and answer-binding completeness; final canonical source verification remains separate after Permanent ID integration.
